## Breaking changes

- Library: `GixorFactory::load_or_default` now returns `Result<Gixor>` instead of `Gixor`, so that a configuration file that cannot be read is reported rather than replaced (#60). `GixorFactory::load_or_new_at` does the same for a given path.
- Library: `impl Default for Gixor` is removed, since `Default` cannot report that the configuration directory is unknown (#61). Use `GixorFactory::new_at(GixorFactory::default_config_path()?)` instead.
- Library: `Error::to_err` is renamed to `Error::error_or`. `Error::error_or_else` is added, taking a closure for the `Ok` value.
- Command: `gixor entries` lists the names with their repository and path, as written in the headings, e.g. `default/Rust` and `default/Global/macOS` rather than `Rust` and `macOS`. The headings `gixor dump` writes name the boilerplates by their paths, so the heading of a boilerplate under a directory, such as `Global/macOS`, changes on the next dump (#92).
- Command: `gixor list` and `gixor search` print the boilerplates by their paths, sorted, e.g. `Global/AL` and `Global/macOS` rather than `AL` and `macOS`, so that boilerplates sharing a name can be told apart and every name in the lists can be passed to `gixor dump` as it is. `gixor search` still matches the query against the file names. Naming a boilerplate by its file name, as in `gixor dump macOS`, keeps working (#93).
- Command: `-H/--header` of `gixor list` is replaced by `--no-header`. `-H` could not turn the headers off, and `gixor list -H` is now rejected as an unknown argument; drop it from scripts. `gixor alias list` no longer accepts `-H/--header`, which it ignored (#55, #78).

## New features

- A boilerplate can be named by its path in the repository, such as `gixor dump Global/AL` or `gixor dump default/Global/AL`, to choose among boilerplates sharing a name (#92).

## Bug fixes

- `gixor list --no-header` prints the boilerplate names without the repository headers (#55, #78).
- gixor no longer panics when the configuration directory cannot be determined, e.g. when `HOME` is not set. It reports an error instead (#61).
- A broken `config.json` is now reported as an error. It used to be replaced by the default configuration without a word, and then overwritten by the next command that stored the configuration, such as `gixor alias add`, losing the settings for good (#60).
- A name shared by several boilerplates, such as `AL` (`AL.gitignore` and `Global/AL.gitignore`) or `Racket`, now always resolves to the same file: the shallowest one, and among those of the same depth the first by path. It used to depend on the order the file system listed the files in, so the same command could write different rules on different machines. A warning names the other candidates (#46).
- `gixor search` now matches regardless of case. A query containing an uppercase letter, such as `gixor search Rust`, used to match nothing (#54, #65).
- Correct the crates.io category name in `Cargo.toml`.

## Improvements

- `RUST_LOG` can add module-specific log levels on top of `--log`, e.g. `RUST_LOG=gixor=trace`. `--log` still sets the overall level, as before (#58, #72).
- `gixor --version` no longer lists Cargo features, which the command has none of: it always said `no features` (#75, #88).

## Documentation

- Replace the Rust Report Card badge with the SonarCloud quality gate badge (#66, #68).

## Development

- Analyze the code with SonarQube (#53).
- Check the formatting with `cargo fmt --check` in CI, and format the existing code (#67, #69).
- Use the release notes in `.github/release-notes/` when creating a release (#70, #71).
- Commit `Cargo.lock`, and build, test and publish with `--locked`, so that every build of a commit uses the same dependency versions. Dependabot keeps the dependencies up to date (#74, #81).
- The build script of the command no longer reads the whole environment, and no longer reruns, recompiling the command, on every build (#75, #88).
